english.title: Destroy / damage property of a value unknown
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse,

(A)_[destroyed **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damaged **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_

(C)_[of a value unknown]_
(D)_[of a value below five hundred pounds, namely **(..SPECIFY VALUE - USE WHEN ISSUING PENALTY NOTICE FOR DISORDER ONLY..)]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording should only be used on those rare occasions when the value of the property damaged cannot be established prior to charge. Post charge, once the value of the damage has been determined this charge must be amended.
(ii) Use offence wording H2081 and H2082 where the value of the damage is known.
(iii) Property damaged/destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(iv) Where the damage is to a memorial (see section 22(11A) and (11D)) the value of the damage is irrelevant to mode of trial and the offence can be tried summarily or on indictment even if the value involved is less than £5000, see section 22(1) of, and Schedule 2 to, the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.
(v) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(vi) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
(vii) The Criminal Justice and Police Act (Amendment) 2001 and Police Reform Act 2002 (Modification) Order 2004 (S.I.2540/2004), provides that Accredited Persons may not issue a penalty notice for disorder for this offence.

other.penalty:
Value under £500-00p:-
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Value £500-00p to £5000-00p:-
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Value over £5000.00p:-
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
